assessments.protocol.lactate.name: Lactate step test
assessments.protocol.lactate.desc: Warm-up with a baseline sample, then {stages} stages of {min} min starting at {start} km/h, {step} km/h faster each stage, {incline} % incline. {sampling}
assessments.desc.pause: After each stage the belt stops for {s} s for the lactate sample.
assessments.desc.on_the_move: The lactate sample is taken on the move; the belt keeps running.
assessments.protocol.maxhr.desc: {warmup} min warm-up, then {how} until the runner cannot go on. Press Exhausted when the runner steps off; heart rate is then recorded for one more minute for recovery. {sprint}
assessments.desc.ramp_incline: constant {speed} km/h, {start} % incline on step 1 and {step} % more every {s} s
assessments.desc.ramp_speed: {step} km/h faster every {s} s at {incline} % incline
assessments.desc.sprint: When the runner has about a minute left you can start a {s} s final sprint, {kmh} km/h faster.
assessments.protocol.combined.name: Lactate step test to max
assessments.protocol.combined.desc: After the last lactate sample the test goes straight into a ramp to max: {speed} km/h, {start} % incline on step 1 and {step} % more every {s} s. One visit gives both the thresholds and max HR.
assessments.protocol.gait.name: Running technique
assessments.protocol.gait.desc: The runner runs {speeds} km/h, {s} s at each speed, {incline} % incline. The camera records and the strides are analysed for each speed.
assessments.error.stages: The test needs at least one stage.
assessments.error.step: The increment and the stage length must be greater than zero.
assessments.error.mode: Unknown ramp: choose incline or speed.
assessments.error.lactate: Lactate must be between 0 and 30 mmol/L.
assessments.error.rpe: Effort (Borg) must be a whole number from 6 to 20.
assessments.error.treadmill: The treadmill is not responding ({err}). Set the speed by hand; the test continues.
assessments.error.crash: The test stopped because of an error. Check the treadmill.
assessments.prompt.aborted: Test aborted. The treadmill is stopping.
assessments.prompt.recovery: Well done! Walk easy, heart rate is recorded for one more minute.
assessments.prompt.hand_change: The belt was set by hand to {target} (planned {planned}).
assessments.prompt.hand_overridden: The belt ran at {was}, set by hand. Now: {target}
assessments.prompt.recovery_manual: Well done! Lower the treadmill to {target} and walk easy, heart rate is recorded for one more minute.
assessments.lactate.error.method: The method {method} could not be calculated for this test.
assessments.lactate.warn.too_few: Only {n} lactate values. At least 3, preferably 5 or more, are needed for thresholds.
assessments.lactate.warn.few_points: Only {n} lactate values: the thresholds are uncertain. More stages give a more reliable curve.
assessments.lactate.warn.incline_varies: The incline changed between stages. Thresholds are based on speed and may be misleading.
assessments.lactate.warn.missing_hr: Heart rate is missing for a stage, so HR at a threshold may be missing.
assessments.lactate.warn.noisy: Lactate drops in the middle of the curve. Check the values (bad sample or sweat on the finger?).
assessments.lactate.warn.no_rise: Lactate rose less than 1 mmol/L. The test was too easy or too short to find the thresholds.
assessments.lactate.warn.fit_failed: No curve could be fitted to the values.
assessments.lactate.warn.poor_fit: The curve fits the values poorly (R² {r2}). Check the values.
assessments.lactate.warn.poly_interpolat: With so few values the polynomial passes straight through the points. The exponential curve is safer.
assessments.lactate.warn.edge: {method} landed at the last stage. The test probably ended too early.
assessments.lactate.warn.obla_not_reache: Lactate never reached 4 mmol/L, so OBLA is missing.
assessments.lactate.warn.method_missing: {method} could not be calculated. Another method is used.
assessments.lactate.warn.order: LT1 is not below LT2. Choose other methods or check the values.
assessments.maxhr.warn.artefacts: {n} faulty heart rate values were removed. Moisten the strap and check that it fits tightly.
assessments.maxhr.warn.gaps: Heart rate is missing for much of the time. Check the strap.
assessments.maxhr.warn.short: The test was too short to see whether heart rate levelled off.
assessments.maxhr.crit.plateau: Heart rate levelled off (at most {bpm} beats higher over the last minute)
assessments.maxhr.crit.age: Close to age-predicted max HR ({pred} bpm)
assessments.maxhr.crit.age_missing: Age missing, no comparison with age-predicted max HR
assessments.maxhr.crit.rpe: Perceived effort 19–20 on the Borg scale
assessments.maxhr.crit.lactate: Lactate at least 8 mmol/L after the test
assessments.compare.shift.right: The lactate curve has shifted right ({kmh} km/h): better endurance.
assessments.compare.shift.left: The lactate curve has shifted left ({kmh} km/h): lower endurance than last time.
assessments.compare.shift.none: The lactate curve is in the same place.
assessments.compare.shift.unknown: The curves cannot be compared (too few common values).
assessments.zones.error.max_hr: Max heart rate is needed for heart rate zones (100–240 bpm).
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I1.name: I1 Easy distance
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I1.purpo: Base training and recovery. Long runs at conversation pace that build the heart, capillaries and fat burning.
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I2.name: I2 Moderate distance
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I2.purpo: Somewhat faster distance. Builds endurance; use sparingly since it tires more than I1 without giving much more.
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I3.name: I3 Threshold
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I3.purpo: Just below the lactate threshold. Intervals (e.g. 4–6 × 6–10 min) that raise threshold speed.
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I4.name: I4 Hard intervals
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I4.purpo: Above threshold, close to maximal oxygen uptake. 3–5 min intervals that raise VO2max.
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I5.name: I5 Very hard intervals
assessments.zones.olympiatoppen.I5.purpo: Close to max. Short intervals (1–3 min) and race pace for short distances.
assessments.zones.seiler.Z1.name: Zone 1 Easy
assessments.zones.seiler.Z1.purpose: Below LT1. Where most (about 80 %) of training should be.
assessments.zones.seiler.Z2.name: Zone 2 Moderate
assessments.zones.seiler.Z2.purpose: Between LT1 and LT2. Tempo and threshold.
assessments.zones.seiler.Z3.name: Zone 3 Hard
assessments.zones.seiler.Z3.purpose: Above LT2. Intervals close to max.
assessments.protocol.lactate.end: The test ends after the last stage or when the runner cannot go on (press Exhausted). Gives LT1, LT2 and the zones.
assessments.lactate.warn.close: LT1 and LT2 landed at almost the same speed, so the test does not separate them. The zones are therefore based on heart rate. More stages, continuing above the threshold, give safer thresholds.
assessments.zones.estimated_long: The zones are estimated from max heart rate: the test gave no thresholds, so the limits are averages and not your own thresholds.
assessments.zonesys.olympiatoppen.name: 5 zones · Olympiatoppen I1–I5
assessments.zonesys.olympiatoppen.note: The Norwegian scale used in Norwegian and Swedish endurance sport. The limits are set at your thresholds: I1 ends at the aerobic threshold (LT1) and I3 ends at the anaerobic threshold (LT2).
assessments.zonesys.seiler.name: 3 zones · Seiler
assessments.zonesys.seiler.note: Three zones with the limits at your two thresholds: below LT1, between the thresholds and above LT2.
assessments.zonesys.swedish.name: 4 zones · Swedish A1–A3+
assessments.zonesys.swedish.note: The Swedish scale: A1 below the aerobic threshold (LT1), A2 between the thresholds, A3 above the anaerobic threshold (LT2) and A3+ the last beats up to max heart rate.
assessments.zonesys.garmin.name: 5 zones · Garmin
assessments.zonesys.garmin.note: Garmin's five zones, placed so that zone 2 ends at your aerobic threshold (LT1) and zone 4 ends at your anaerobic threshold (LT2).
assessments.zonesys.polar.name: 5 zones · Polar
assessments.zonesys.polar.note: Polar always sets the zones in fixed steps of 10 % of max heart rate, wherever your thresholds are.
assessments.zonesys.friel.name: 7 zones · Friel
assessments.zonesys.friel.note: Joe Friel's running zones, in per cent of the threshold heart rate. The heart rate at your anaerobic threshold (LT2) is used as threshold heart rate.
assessments.zones.swedish.A1.name: Low intensity
assessments.zones.swedish.A1.purpose: Easy distance at talking pace. The base of all endurance training.
assessments.zones.swedish.A2.name: Medium intensity
assessments.zones.swedish.A2.purpose: Brisk distance and tempo, between the thresholds.
assessments.zones.swedish.A3.name: High intensity
assessments.zones.swedish.A3.purpose: Intervals and race pace, above the threshold.
assessments.zones.swedish.A3+.name: Maximal
assessments.zones.swedish.A3+.purpose: Short, very hard intervals. Heart rate often lags behind, so go by pace and feel.
assessments.zones.garmin.Z1.name: Warm up
assessments.zones.garmin.Z2.name: Easy
assessments.zones.garmin.Z2.purpose: Easy distance. Most of the training belongs here.
assessments.zones.garmin.Z3.name: Aerobic
assessments.zones.garmin.Z4.name: Threshold
assessments.zones.garmin.Z5.name: Maximum
assessments.zones.polar.Z1.name: Very light
assessments.zones.polar.Z2.name: Light
assessments.zones.polar.Z3.name: Moderate
assessments.zones.polar.Z4.name: Hard
assessments.zones.polar.Z5.name: Maximum
assessments.zones.friel.Z1.name: Recovery
assessments.zones.friel.Z2.name: Aerobic
assessments.zones.friel.Z3.name: Tempo
assessments.zones.friel.Z4.name: Sub-threshold
assessments.zones.friel.Z5a.name: Super-threshold
assessments.zones.friel.Z5a.purpose: Threshold intervals and 10 km race pace.
assessments.zones.friel.Z5b.name: Aerobic capacity
assessments.zones.friel.Z5c.name: Anaerobic capacity
assessments.garmin.title: Set up your watch
assessments.garmin.intro_lthr: Open the heart rate zones in Garmin Connect or on the watch. Choose zones based on lactate threshold heart rate (% LTHR) and enter these values. The watch then follows the test: zone 2 ends at your aerobic threshold (LT1) and zone 4 ends at your anaerobic threshold (LT2).
assessments.garmin.intro_max: The test gave no lactate thresholds. Open the heart rate zones in Garmin Connect or on the watch, enter the max heart rate and let the zones follow % of max heart rate. The zones are estimated from max heart rate; a lactate test gives your own limits.
assessments.garmin.why_title: Why does the watch show other zones?
assessments.garmin.why: By default the watch sets the zones at fixed percentages of max heart rate: 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90 %. Those percentages are averages for many people. The test measured where your own thresholds are, and they seldom sit exactly on the average. That is why two people with the same max heart rate can have different zones, and why the watch differs from the test until you have entered the values.
assessments.garmin.rest_missing: missing: measure it lying down on a calm morning
assessments.garmin.not_measured: not measured: keep the watch's own value
assessments.vo2max.title: Estimated VO2max
assessments.vo2max.disclaimer: Estimated from the speed and heart rate of the test. Only a real VO2max test that measures the breathing gases can tell for certain.
assessments.vo2max.method.acsm_final_sta: Last completed stage of the max test (ACSM running equation)
assessments.vo2max.method.hr_extrapolati: Heart rate and speed of the stages, extended to max heart rate
assessments.vo2max.method.uth_sorensen: Max heart rate divided by resting heart rate (Uth–Sørensen)
assessments.info.lactate.title: Lactate step test
assessments.info.lactate.measures: How much lactate you have in your blood at different speeds. It shows your two thresholds: the speed where lactate starts to rise (aerobic threshold, LT1) and the highest speed you can hold for long without lactate running away (anaerobic threshold, LT2).
assessments.info.lactate.how: You warm up and then run 6–8 stages of 4 minutes, a little faster for each stage. After each stage a drop of blood is taken from your finger. You do not have to run to your limit.
assessments.info.lactate.equipment: Treadmill, heart rate strap and a lactate meter with test strips.
assessments.info.lactate.standard: Step test at 1 % incline, which matches running outdoors. LT1 is set where lactate has risen 1.0 mmol/l above your lowest value. LT2 is calculated with the modified Dmax method (Bishop 1998). The coach can change method, for example to a fixed 4 mmol/l, to compare with other tests.
assessments.info.lactate.get: Speed, pace and heart rate at both thresholds, the lactate curve, your training zones and a comparison with your previous test.
assessments.info.lactate.limits: The thresholds are approximate and reflect the day's form. Different methods give different answers, and the meter has a margin of error. Sleep, food, heat and hard training the day before all matter. Compare tests that were done the same way.
assessments.info.max_hr.title: Max heart rate test
assessments.info.max_hr.measures: Your highest heart rate: how fast your heart beats when you go all out.
assessments.info.max_hr.how: After a 10-minute warm-up the incline or speed goes up every minute until you cannot go on, usually after 8–12 minutes. Then you walk for a minute while your heart rate is measured.
assessments.info.max_hr.equipment: Treadmill and a chest heart rate strap.
assessments.info.max_hr.standard: Max heart rate is the highest 5-second average, so single false beats do not count. The program judges whether it was your true maximum by four accepted signs: heart rate levelled off, it was close to the age-predicted value (208 − 0.7 × age), you rated the effort 19–20 on the Borg scale (6–20) and lactate was at least 8 mmol/l. At least two must be met.
assessments.info.max_hr.get: Max heart rate, how much it dropped in the first minute afterwards, and heart rate zones.
assessments.info.max_hr.limits: The test requires an all-out effort. If you are not used to that or have a bad day, the value comes out too low. Max heart rate in running does not apply to cycling or swimming. If you have heart problems or are unsure, ask a doctor first.
assessments.info.gait.title: Running technique analysis
assessments.info.gait.measures: How you run: steps per minute (cadence), how far in front of the body the foot lands (overstride), shin angle, knee bend, trunk lean, bounce and how much the hip drops.
assessments.info.gait.how: You run at 2–3 speeds, two minutes each, while a camera films from the side or from behind. The program finds your joints in every frame and measures the steps.
assessments.info.gait.equipment: Treadmill and a camera, for example a GoPro.
assessments.info.gait.standard: The joints are found in the image with MediaPipe Pose from Google (33 points on the body). The values are compared with reference values from research on running technique in recreational runners. The reference values show what is common, not what is right for everyone.
assessments.info.gait.get: Still images with the deviations circled, your values against the reference values and a few things to think about, each with a drill.
assessments.info.gait.limits: Video from one angle shows the movement in two dimensions. Angles can be off by a few degrees if the camera is not square, and rotations do not show. The analysis is a basis for training. It is not a medical examination and does not replace a laboratory with 3D cameras.
assessments.info.zones.title: Training zones
assessments.info.zones.measures: Zones divide training by how hard it is. They are not a test of their own, but are calculated from the lactate step test, the max heart rate test or the test Heart rate and speed zones.
assessments.info.zones.how: The program sets the zone limits at your thresholds. You choose the system you want to see, and get the same thresholds converted to it.
assessments.info.zones.standard: The default is the Olympiatoppen scale with five zones (I1–I5), used in Norwegian and Swedish endurance sport. The same thresholds can be shown as three zones (Seiler), Swedish A1–A3+, Garmin's or Polar's five zones and Friel's seven zones.
assessments.info.zones.get: Heart rate and pace for each zone, a comparison between the systems and a box with the values to enter in your Garmin watch.
assessments.info.zones.limits: After a max heart rate test alone the zones are estimated from max heart rate and built on averages, not on your thresholds. Heart rate rises in heat, uphill and when you are tired, so the same zone can feel different from day to day.
assessments.info.vo2max.title: Estimated VO2max
assessments.info.vo2max.measures: VO2max is the largest amount of oxygen the body can take up per minute and kilo of body weight (ml/kg/min), a measure of fitness. Here it is not measured, it is estimated.
assessments.info.vo2max.how: Not a test of its own. The value is calculated from the speed, incline and heart rate of the max heart rate test or the lactate step test.
assessments.info.vo2max.standard: After a test to the limit, the speed and incline of the last stage you completed are used, with the running equation from the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM). After a lactate step test, the relation between heart rate and speed is extended to your max heart rate. With heart rate only, max heart rate divided by resting heart rate is used (Uth and Sørensen 2004).
assessments.info.vo2max.get: An estimated value with a range, and which method was used.
assessments.info.vo2max.limits: Estimated from the speed and heart rate of the test. Only a real VO2max test that measures the breathing gases can tell for certain. The error is often 10–15 %, so the value is good for following your own progress but not for comparing yourself with others.
assessments.prompt.recovery_panel: The belt was stopped. Recovery heart rate is measured for a minute, stand still or walk easy.
assessments.prompt.ramp_speed: The treadmill is at its highest incline ({incline} %): the speed rises {step} km/h per step instead.
assessments.prompt.ramp_incline: The treadmill is at its top speed ({speed} km/h): the incline rises {step} % per step instead.
assessments.prompt.ramp_at_max: The treadmill is at its top speed and incline ({target}). The load cannot rise any more: keep going as long as you can.
assessments.desc.overflow_speed: When the treadmill reaches its highest incline, the speed rises {step} km/h per step instead.
assessments.desc.overflow_incline: When the treadmill reaches its top speed, the incline rises {step} % per step instead.
assessments.desc.sprint_auto: The final sprint starts by itself: {s} s at {kmh} km/h faster when the heart rate has levelled off (after at least 4 min of ramp) or after 12 min of ramp. It is the last step of the ramp.
assessments.vo2max.none: Cannot be estimated from this test.
assessments.vo2max.reason.not_max: The test probably did not reach max heart rate (the max criteria were not met), so the last stage says nothing certain about your highest oxygen uptake.
assessments.vo2max.reason.steep: The last stage was steeper than {deg} %. The running equation (ACSM) overestimates there, so it is not used.
assessments.vo2max.reason.short: The last stage was shorter than {s} s. The equation needs a steady pace, so it is not used.
assessments.vo2max.reason.implausible: An estimate was more than {pct} % from the value from max and resting heart rate and is not shown.
assessments.vo2max.watch_differs: The test's estimate differs {pct} % from the watch's (more than {limit} %). Trust a test with gas analysis more than either.
assessments.maxhr.basis.this_test: The zones are built on the max heart rate from this test, {bpm} bpm.
assessments.maxhr.basis.saved_max: The zones are built on your saved max heart rate {bpm} bpm ({origin}).
assessments.maxhr.basis.peak_not_max: The test's peak was {peak} and probably did not reach max.
assessments.protocol.hrzones.name: Heart rate and speed zones
assessments.protocol.hrzones.name_previo: Heart rate and speed zones, from the last test
assessments.protocol.hrzones.desc: {warmup} min warm-up, then {stages} steps of {min} min at an even speed starting at {start} km/h and {step} km/h faster for each step, with no pauses and no blood samples. Right after the last step the speed rises {ramp} km/h every {s} seconds until the runner cannot go on. The incline is {incline} % all through the test. The test runs by itself: when the belt is stopped on the panel it ends, and the heart rate is measured for one more minute.
assessments.hrzones.warn.unstable: The heart rate did not settle at {steps} km/h: it rose more than {bpm} beats during the last minute of the step. The step therefore counts less in the relation. The speed was probably above your threshold, or the step was too short.
assessments.hrzones.warn.short: The step at {steps} km/h was shorter than {min} minutes and is not counted: the heart rate does not have time to settle.
assessments.hrzones.warn.no_ramp: The test ended before the ramp to max. The highest heart rate of the test is therefore not a max heart rate.
assessments.hrzones.warn.too_few: Only {n} steps can be used. At least {need} are needed for a relation between heart rate and speed, so the zones get no speed.
assessments.hrzones.warn.narrow: The heart rate differs by less than {bpm} beats between the easiest and the hardest step. That is not enough for a relation between heart rate and speed.
assessments.hrzones.warn.not_rising: The heart rate did not rise with the speed in the steps, so no relation could be computed. Check the heart rate strap.
assessments.hrzones.warn.poor_fit: The steps do not follow a straight line very well. The speeds of the zones are less certain than usual.
assessments.hrzones.quality.good: Good relation: {n} steps, R² {r2}, the steps lie ±{see} bpm from the line.
assessments.hrzones.quality.fair: Acceptable relation: {n} steps, R² {r2}, the steps lie ±{see} bpm from the line.
assessments.hrzones.quality.poor: Weak relation: {n} steps, R² {r2}, the steps lie ±{see} bpm from the line.
assessments.hrzones.speed_from_hr: Speed from heart rate, not from lactate
assessments.hrzones.speed_from_hr_long: The speeds are estimated from the relation between heart rate and speed in the steps of the test. No lactate was measured, so the borders of the zones are per cent of max heart rate and not your thresholds.
assessments.hrzones.extrapolated: ≈ means that the speed lies outside the measured steps ({lo}–{hi} km/h) and is extended along the line, at most {km} km/h outside. Further out no speed is given.
assessments.info.hr_zones.title: Heart rate and speed zones
assessments.info.hr_zones.measures: Your max heart rate and the speed that belongs to each heart rate zone, with no blood samples and no lactate meter.
assessments.info.hr_zones.how: After the warm-up you run 4–5 steps of 4 minutes at an even speed, each a little faster, with no pauses. Then the speed rises 0.5 km/h every minute until you cannot go on. The incline stays at 1 %. When you stop the belt the test ends by itself.
assessments.info.hr_zones.equipment: Treadmill and a chest heart rate strap. A camera to film technique.
assessments.info.hr_zones.standard: Heart rate lags speed by 2–3 minutes, so each step counts the mean of its last minute, and a step where it then rises more than 3 beats counts less. The relation is a straight line through the steps. Max heart rate is judged as in the max heart rate test. The zones are Garmin's five in per cent of max heart rate, and the line gives the speed at each border.
assessments.info.hr_zones.get: The max heart rate, heart rate zones with speed and pace, the heart rate of each step, a measure of how good the relation is and an estimated VO2max.
assessments.info.hr_zones.limits: The speeds are estimated from heart rate, not from lactate: the test does not find your thresholds. Speeds outside the measured steps are only extended a little and are marked with ≈. Heat, fluid, sleep and caffeine affect heart rate from day to day. The speeds hold for a treadmill at 1 % incline.
assessments.info.bike_lactate.title: Lactate step test on the bike
assessments.info.bike_lactate.measures: The lactate in your blood at different powers on the bike. It shows your two thresholds in watts: the power where lactate starts to rise (LT1) and the highest power you can hold for a long time without lactate running away (LT2).
assessments.info.bike_lactate.how: You warm up for 10 minutes and then ride 6–8 stages of 5 minutes. The trainer holds the power, which rises 25–30 W each stage. In the last half minute of each stage a drop of blood is taken from a finger or the ear lobe while you keep pedalling.
assessments.info.bike_lactate.equipment: Smart trainer that holds the power (ERG mode), heart rate strap and lactate meter.
assessments.info.bike_lactate.standard: The same methods as the running step test: LT1 where lactate has risen 1.0 mmol/L above your lowest value, LT2 by modified Dmax (Bishop 1998). Stages of 5 minutes and the starting power are our own design, not a published protocol.
assessments.info.bike_lactate.get: Power, W/kg and heart rate at both thresholds, the lactate curve against power, your cycling zones in heart rate and watts, and a comparison with your previous bike test.
assessments.info.bike_lactate.limits: The thresholds apply to cycling. Shorter stages give higher threshold watts, so only compare tests with the same stage length. The trainer's power reading has an error of a few per cent. Sleep, food, heat and hard training the day before all matter.
assessments.info.bike_ramp.title: Ramp test on the bike
assessments.info.bike_ramp.measures: Your highest heart rate on the bike, your best one-minute power and an estimated FTP: the power you can hold for about an hour.
assessments.info.bike_ramp.how: After a 10-minute warm-up the power rises 20–25 W every minute until you cannot pedal any more, usually after 10–15 minutes. The test ends by itself when you stop pedalling, and heart rate is measured for one more minute.
assessments.info.bike_ramp.equipment: Smart trainer that holds the power (ERG mode) and a heart rate strap.
assessments.info.bike_ramp.standard: The best minute is the highest average power over 60 seconds, and FTP is estimated as 75 % of it. Max heart rate is the highest 5-second average and is judged by the same signs as the treadmill max test, except age, which belongs to running.
assessments.info.bike_ramp.get: Your max heart rate on the bike, best one-minute power, an estimated FTP with W/kg and Coggan's seven power zones.
assessments.info.bike_ramp.limits: FTP from a ramp test can come out too high for riders with a strong sprint. Max heart rate on the bike is usually lower than in running and is kept apart. The test requires an all-out effort. If you have heart problems or are unsure: ask a doctor first.
assessments.info.bike_ftp.title: FTP test, 20 minutes
assessments.info.bike_ftp.measures: Your FTP (Functional Threshold Power): the power you can hold for about an hour. It is used to steer training on the bike.
assessments.info.bike_ftp.how: You warm up for 15 minutes while the trainer holds the power. Then you ride 20 minutes as hard as you can hold evenly. The trainer lets go of the power and rides like a flat road, and you choose the power yourself with gears and cadence.
assessments.info.bike_ftp.equipment: Smart trainer and heart rate strap.
assessments.info.bike_ftp.standard: FTP is 95 % of the best average power over 20 continuous minutes. The power zones are Coggan's seven, in per cent of FTP: below 55, 55–75, 76–90, 91–105, 106–120, 121–150 and above 150 %. If the power fell more than 8 % between the first and second half, the result says so.
assessments.info.bike_ftp.get: FTP in watts and W/kg, best one-minute power, the power zones and heart rate during the test.
assessments.info.bike_ftp.limits: FTP is an estimate with an error of about 3–5 %, and not the same number as the threshold (LT2) from a lactate test. An uneven effort gives too low a value. The test needs all 20 minutes: a test that is cut short gives no FTP.
assessments.info.bikefit.title: Bike fit
assessments.info.bikefit.measures: How you sit on the bike: the knee angle at the bottom and top of the pedal stroke, hip angle, trunk angle, shoulder and elbow, how much the hips move, and the knee's track seen from the front.
assessments.info.bikefit.how: Your bike is on the trainer. After a 5-minute warm-up you are filmed for 2–3 minutes at a steady working power, from the side and the front. The program finds the joints in each frame and measures the pedal strokes. The coach checks mobility, feet, cleats and bike measurements by hand.
assessments.info.bikefit.equipment: Smart trainer, one or two cameras with at least 60 frames/s, and a goniometer.
assessments.info.bikefit.standard: The joints are found with Google's MediaPipe Pose. The knee angle at the bottom is compared with the published range 33–43°. The other reference values are bike fitting practice and are marked as such. Every value is shown with its measurement error.
assessments.info.bikefit.get: Frames from the pedal stroke with the angles drawn in, the measurements against reference values, suggestions for saddle height, cleats and stem, and the manual check-up.
assessments.info.bikefit.limits: Video measures in two dimensions and only the leg nearest the camera. A suggestion smaller than the measurement error is marked uncertain. Move the saddle at most 5 mm at a time. For road bikes, and no substitute for an examination if you have pain.
assessments.info.bike_zones.title: Cycling zones
assessments.info.bike_zones.measures: Heart rate and power zones for training on the bike. Not a test of their own: they are calculated from the bike tests.
assessments.info.bike_zones.how: After a lactate test the zone borders are set at your thresholds, in heart rate and watts. After an FTP or ramp test Coggan's power zones are calculated in per cent of FTP. The ramp test also gives your max heart rate on the bike.
assessments.info.bike_zones.standard: The same zone systems as for running can be chosen, for example Olympiatoppen's five zones (I1–I5), Seiler's three zones or Garmin's five. The power zones from FTP are Coggan's seven.
assessments.info.bike_zones.get: The zones in heart rate and power, and your max heart rate on the bike kept on its own.
assessments.info.bike_zones.limits: Heart rate is usually lower on the bike than in running, and by how much differs between people. Running's max heart rate and thresholds are therefore never used for cycling. Without a bike test of your own the zones rest only on the test's peak heart rate, and the result says so.
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.title: Lactate step test on the SkiErg
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.measures: The lactate in your blood at different powers in double poling. It shows your two thresholds in watts and as pace per 500 metres: LT1, where lactate starts to rise, and LT2, the highest you can hold for a long time without lactate running away.
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.how: After a 10-minute warm-up you pole 6–8 stages of 4 minutes, 15–20 W more each stage. The target is on the TV and on the monitor, and you hold it yourself. After each stage a drop of blood is taken during a half-minute pause.
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.equipmen: Concept2 SkiErg with the PM5 monitor, heart rate strap and lactate meter.
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.standard: A SkiErg cannot be controlled, so each stage counts the power you actually held, leaving out the first 15 seconds. The thresholds are calculated as in running: LT1 1.0 mmol/L above the lowest value, LT2 by modified Dmax. There is no published SkiErg protocol, so the stages are our own design.
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.get: Power, pace per 500 m and heart rate at both thresholds, the lactate curve, zones in heart rate, watts and pace, and a comparison with your previous test.
assessments.info.skierg_lactate.limits: Threshold heart rate is lower in double poling than in running, so the zones apply to poling only. The damper setting matters: keep it the same between tests; the drag factor is in the report. A stage far from its target makes the curve less certain. Sleep, food and hard training the day before matter.
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.title: Ramp test on the SkiErg
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.measures: Your highest heart rate in double poling and your best one-minute power.
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.how: After a 10-minute warm-up the target rises 15–20 W every minute until you cannot go on. The test ends by itself when you stop poling, and heart rate is measured for a while longer.
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.equipment: Concept2 SkiErg with the PM5 monitor and a heart rate strap.
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.standard: The highest heart rate is the highest 5-second average. The best minute is the highest average power over 60 seconds, with the pace per 500 m by Concept2's formula. FTP is not calculated, because the formula is made for cycling.
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.get: Your highest heart rate in double poling and best one-minute power with pace per 500 m.
assessments.info.skierg_ramp.limits: Arms and trunk often tire before heart rate reaches its max, so the highest heart rate in poling is usually lower than in running and is kept apart. The test requires an all-out effort. If you have heart problems or are unsure: ask a doctor first.
assessments.info.ski_technique.title: Double poling technique
assessments.info.ski_technique.measures: How you pole on the SkiErg: hand height and elbow angle at the start, trunk, hip and knee flexion at the end of the pull, whether the trunk leads the arms, and the rhythm of pull and recovery.
assessments.info.ski_technique.how: After a 5-minute warm-up you are filmed from the side for 2 minutes at a steady rate, at a power you can hold with good technique. The program finds the joints in each frame, splits the film into strokes and measures each one.
assessments.info.ski_technique.equipment: Concept2 SkiErg and a camera with at least 60 frames/s.
assessments.info.ski_technique.standard: The joints are found with Google's MediaPipe Pose. Research on double poling is done on snow and roller skis and gives directions, not degrees for the SkiErg. All reference values are therefore practice values and marked as such, and every value is shown with its measurement error.
assessments.info.ski_technique.get: Frames from the stroke with deviations circled, the measurements against reference values, something to think about with an exercise, and from the second test a comparison with last time.
assessments.info.ski_technique.limits: Video from the side measures in two dimensions, and angles can be a few degrees off if the camera is not square. The reference values show what usually works, not what is right for everyone. Technique on the SkiErg is not the same as on snow.
assessments.info.skierg_zones.title: SkiErg zones
assessments.info.skierg_zones.measures: Heart rate and power zones for double poling training. Not a test of their own: they are calculated from the SkiErg tests.
assessments.info.skierg_zones.how: After a lactate test the zone borders are set at your thresholds, in heart rate, watts and pace per 500 m. The ramp test gives your highest heart rate in poling.
assessments.info.skierg_zones.standard: The same zone systems as for running can be chosen, for example Olympiatoppen's five zones (I1–I5), Seiler's three zones or Garmin's five. Watts and pace follow Concept2: watts = 2.80 / (seconds per metre)³.
assessments.info.skierg_zones.get: The zones in heart rate, watts and pace per 500 m, and your highest heart rate in poling kept on its own.
assessments.info.skierg_zones.limits: Threshold heart rate is clearly lower in double poling than in running: a study of elite skiers found about 161 against 187 beats per minute (Larson 2006). The difference is personal, so running zones are never used for the SkiErg. Without a test of your own the result says so.
assessments.prompt.free_target: as hard as you can hold all the way (aim at {target})
assessments.prompt.bike.aborted: The test was stopped. The trainer releases the resistance.
assessments.prompt.bike.recovery: Well done! Pedal easily, the heart rate is measured for one more minute.
assessments.prompt.bike.recovery_panel: You stopped pedalling, so the test is over. Pedal easily, the heart rate is measured for one more minute.
assessments.prompt.bike.ramp_at_max: The trainer is at its highest power ({target}). The load cannot rise further: go on as long as you can.
assessments.prompt.bike.crash: The test stopped because of an error. Check the trainer.
assessments.prompt.skierg.recovery: Well done! Ski easily or stand still, the heart rate is measured for one more minute.
assessments.prompt.skierg.recovery_panel: You stopped skiing, so the test is over. The heart rate is measured for one more minute.
assessments.prompt.skierg.ramp_at_max: The target cannot rise further ({target}): go on as long as you can.
assessments.prompt.skierg.crash: The test stopped because of an error. Check the connection to the monitor.
assessments.error.ergometer: The device does not answer ({err}). Hold the power yourself, the test goes on.
assessments.desc.pause_bike: After each stage the trainer releases the resistance for {s} s for the lactate sample.
assessments.desc.on_the_move_bike: The lactate sample is taken while the rider keeps pedalling, in the last 30 seconds of the stage.
assessments.desc.pause_skierg: After each stage there is a {s} s pause for the lactate sample.
assessments.desc.on_the_move_skierg: The lactate sample is taken from the ear with as short a break as possible.
assessments.protocol.bike.lactate.name: Lactate step test, cycling
assessments.protocol.bike.lactate.desc: Warm-up with a resting value, then {stages} stages of {min} min starting at {start} W and {step} W more for each stage. The trainer holds the power (ERG mode), so the rider only chooses the cadence: keep about the same cadence through the test. {sampling}
assessments.protocol.bike.lactate.end: The test ends after the last stage or when the rider cannot go on (press Exhausted). Gives LT1 and LT2 in watt and W/kg, and the zones for cycling.
assessments.protocol.bike.ramp.name: Ramp test, cycling (max HR and FTP)
assessments.protocol.bike.ramp.desc: {warmup} min warm-up, then {start} W and {step} W more every {s} seconds until the rider cannot go on. The test ends by itself when the rider stops pedalling, and the heart rate is measured for one more minute. Gives the highest heart rate on the bike, the best one-minute power (MAP) and FTP as 75 % of it.
assessments.protocol.bike.ftp20.name: FTP 20 minutes
assessments.protocol.bike.ftp20.desc: {warmup} min warm-up in ERG mode, then {min} min as hard as the rider can hold all the way. The trainer holds no power in that stage: the rider chooses with gears and cadence, with {target} W to aim at. FTP is 95 % of the mean power.
assessments.protocol.skierg.lactate.name: Lactate step test, SkiErg
Lactate step test, SkiErg, {level}
assessments.protocol.skierg.lactate.desc: Warm-up with a resting value, then {stages} stages of {min} min starting at {start} W and {step} W more for each stage. A SkiErg cannot be set: the screen shows the target and the athlete holds it, and the thresholds are computed on the power that was actually held. {sampling}
assessments.protocol.skierg.lactate.end: The test ends after the last stage or when the athlete cannot hold the target (press Exhausted). Gives LT1 and LT2 in watt and pace per 500 m, and the zones for SkiErg.
assessments.protocol.skierg.ramp.name: Ramp test, SkiErg (highest heart rate)
assessments.protocol.skierg.ramp.desc: {warmup} min warm-up, then {start} W and a {step} W higher target every {s} seconds until the athlete cannot go on. The test ends by itself when the athlete stops, and the heart rate is measured for one more minute. Gives the highest heart rate in double poling and the best one-minute power.
assessments.lactate.warn.same_load: {n} stages were at almost the same power as another stage and count as one (the later sample is used).
assessments.maxhr.crit.age_other_sport: The age criterion belongs to running and is not judged here: the peak heart rate is lower on a bike and in double poling.
assessments.compare.shift.right_load: The lactate curve has moved to the right ({delta} {unit}): better endurance.
assessments.compare.shift.left_load: The lactate curve has moved to the left ({delta} {unit}): poorer endurance than last time.
assessments.power.warn.short: The test has only {min} min of continuous work. FTP from the 20 minute test needs the full 20 minutes and is not computed.
assessments.power.warn.uneven: The power fell {pct} % from the first half to the second. A more even effort gives a safer FTP.
assessments.power.warn.no_power: No power was measured in the test (manual mode), so FTP and the best one-minute power cannot be computed.
assessments.power.method.ftp20: 95 % of the mean power of 20 minutes
assessments.power.method.ramp: 75 % of the best one-minute power of the ramp test
assessments.maxhr.basis.test_top: No max HR is saved. The border of the top zone is built on the highest heart rate of the test, {bpm} bpm, which is not a max HR.
assessments.garmin.sport_bike: The values are for cycling: enter them for the sport cycling in the watch, not as the running or default zones.
assessments.error.film_len: The filmed stage must be at least 30 seconds and the power above zero.
assessments.protocol.bike.bikefit.name: Bike fit, road
assessments.protocol.bike.bikefit.desc: {warmup} min warm-up in ERG mode that is not filmed, then {min} min at {w} W with the hands on the hoods. That stage is filmed from the side, and from the front with a second camera. The position changes with the load, so the power should be one the rider trains at, not easy spinning.
assessments.protocol.skierg.ski.name: Double poling technique
assessments.protocol.skierg.ski.desc: {warmup} min warm-up that is not filmed, then {min} min at an even rate at {w} W. That stage is filmed from the side. The athlete holds the target shown on the TV and stands on the same taped spot every time, so that tests can be compared.
